clue.text: Given option, is standing

indicators.note: taken in the sense 'given a new form', so the following letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone offered a choice is left standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is the anagram signal: OPTION and IS are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing is one's rank or status in society, a synonym.

clue.text: A steep requirement for converting foreign currency

indicators.note: converting changes the form of something, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steep charge is made for changing money abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converting' signals the anagram of A STEEP; 'requirement for' is link padding fitting the money-changing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the monetary unit of Spain before the euro.

clue.text: Gets agitated about a flight

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece sits round the other

parts.note: something that gets agitated stirs

explanation.surface: Someone becomes nervous before boarding a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts STIRS round A. The surface flight is a plane journey; the defining flight is a set of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a continuous series of steps between floors.

clue.text: There's much abuse when one's involved in commerce

indicators.note: being involved in something puts you inside it, so one letter goes within the other word

parts.note: commerce is trade
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A remark about how business attracts plenty of insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' places I (one) inside TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of denunciation pours out a great deal of abuse.

clue.text: Her view got misrepresented-a personal problem

indicators.note: misrepresented means presented wrongly, so the letters of the three words come out in a different order

explanation.surface: A woman's opinion has been distorted, which she takes personally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' signals the anagram of HER VIEW GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying too much body weight is a difficulty that belongs to the individual, a cryptic way of describing it.

clue.text: Some actor portraying indolence

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer plays the part of laziness on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals letters taken from inside 'actor portraying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor is sluggish inactivity, a synonym of laziness.

clue.text: The big guns love the way an establishment will accept direction

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
way gives RD, the abbreviation for road
N is north, a compass direction
taken as written
CE is the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: Artillery adore how an institution will take orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will accept' is loose linking: N is taken on before AN and CE. The Establishment as the Church of England (CE) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military artillery, the heavy guns of an army.

clue.text: Quiet charm going together with taste

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly
to charm is to enchant

explanation.surface: Understated allure goes hand in hand with refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going together with' simply joins P and ENCHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or fondness, as in a taste for something.

clue.text: Held back, being rather unsociable

explanation.surface: Someone kept at a distance because they are not very outgoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tables or seats kept aside are booked in advance; a shy, reticent person is described the same way.

clue.text: Inexperienced in the main?

parts.note: the main is the open ocean, so someone a novice out on it is a green sailor; the phrase is also a bluish-green colour

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour name read literally as a novice at sailing, since green means untried.

clue.text: A girl's hold over a handsome young man

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: Di is a girl's name; with the 's it gives DIS
over can mean on, as in on top of

explanation.surface: A woman has a grip on an attractive youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' puts DIS round ON, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was a beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, hence any good-looking young man.

clue.text: Refuse to arrange a bed for the night

definitions.text: to arrange a bed for the night

explanation.surface: A guest declines hotel room service at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turndown' is the hotel service of folding back the sheets in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject an offer is to decline it; folding back the covers ready for sleep is the hotel bedtime service of the same name.

clue.text: He'll serve stout to a woman

parts.note: stout means fat
her is the pronoun used for a woman as object

explanation.surface: A barman will pour a pint of Guinness for a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the drink but means overweight. A priest is addressed as Father, and serves his parish.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest ministers to his parishioners and is called by this title.

clue.text: Awfully evil note is appearing in entertainment

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something very wicked is noted in the show business world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' signals the anagram of EVIL NOTE IS; 'appearing in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Television is a broadcast medium watched for amusement.

clue.text: Becoming green, screen alteration required unacceptable behaviour

indicators.note: taken as needing or taking in, so the word for misconduct holds the other letters

parts.note: a vice is an immoral or unacceptable habit

indicators.note: an alteration is a change, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changing a screen to green was needed after bad conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alteration' turns SCREEN into RESCEN, which 'required' puts inside VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Virescence is the botanical term for the state of turning verdant.

clue.text: Bill a junior minister presented? That's right

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, which a bill is
a curate is an assistant to a parish priest, a junior clergyman

explanation.surface: A bill is presented by a lesser government member, and that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior minister' looks political but is a church minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct, as right does.

clue.text: Such answers split very big set-up

parts.note: to rip is to split or tear
OS is outsize, a clothing size

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

explanation.surface: Retorts break apart an enormous scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SET to TES in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripostes are quick, sharp retorts, a kind of reply.

clue.text: Point to publication which is revolting

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
an edition is an issue of a publication

explanation.surface: Someone indicates a disgusting magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting means rebellious here, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is conduct inciting rebellion against authority.

clue.text: Where cases are put down in the station

definitions.text: Where cases are put down in the station

parts.words: Where cases are put down in the station
parts.note: cases are criminal cases written down at a police station, not luggage set down at a railway station

explanation.definitionFit: The police record of offences charged is where criminal cases are entered.

clue.text: Paddy's cool

explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' is British informal for a fit of anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a fit of rage; to cool or moderate something is to tone it down.

clue.text: Wind up article giving lead

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Finish the story with a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' looks like a phrasal verb but is GALE plus the reversal signal for AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Galena is the chief ore of the metal Pb.

clue.text: Deal with the bench

explanation.surface: Handle the magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is a high-backed wooden seat; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve a matter is to handle it; an old wooden seat with a high back is also so called.

clue.text: More idealistic society

parts.note: reads as a comparative, but Sir Thomas More wrote of an imaginary perfect state

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More's 1516 book describes an imaginary island with a perfect social order.

clue.text: Current time trial?

parts.note: tide is an old word for time or season, as in Yuletide
a race is a trial of speed

explanation.surface: A cyclist's present race against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Current is a noun here, a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong, fast flow of sea water through a channel is this kind of stream.

clue.text: In Northern Ireland an industrious worker has the edge

parts.note: the ant is proverbially hard-working
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A hard-working Ulster labourer has an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: County Antrim lies in the north-east of Ulster, within the UK province.

clue.text: The easiest word may be misspelt

indicators.note: says the word that follows may become something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The most straightforward word is easy to spell wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals the anagram of MISSPELT.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of plain or uncomplicated means least difficult.

clue.text: Notes to croon-so soothing

parts.note: E and A are musical notes
to croon is to sing softly

explanation.surface: Lullaby music sung gently to calm someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing pain is relieving or calming it.

clue.text: Swell popular with the fold

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a crease is a fold

explanation.surface: A fine fellow liked by the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: Swell is a verb meaning grow, not a fine gentleman; the fold is not a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow larger is to rise in size or amount.
